title: Who handles the repeat job?
hook: A toy owner delegates repeated work. What happens to the new handoff station?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Calculate the new constraint after work is redistributed away from an owner.

misconception: Removing owner work guarantees that the delegated step has unlimited capacity.
objective: Calculate the new constraint after work is redistributed away from an owner.

claims.text: The named work is The E-Myth Revisited, by Michael E. Gerber, candidate publication year 1995.
claims.source: Michael E. Gerber, The E-Myth Revisited (1995); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: The E-Myth Revisited distinguishes building repeatable operating systems from relying on the owner to do every job.
claims.source: Michael E. Gerber, The E-Myth Revisited (1995); chapter (unconfirmed); edition and bibliography not independently opened. Access hold F1.

claims.text: Original stipulated serial line: A capacities [3,10,10] give min(3,10,10)=3 jobs/hour; B capacities [6,5,10] give min(6,5,10)=5 jobs/hour. Every job passes all three stations. In B they handle 6, 5 and 10 jobs/hour. How many completed jobs per hour can B sustain? Every job passes all three stations. A completes {A} jobs/hour; B completes {B}. In B, the owner can pass six per hour, but the handoff handles only five. More than five cannot finish. Real delegation outcomes are not estimated.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response. Builder clarification responding to independent learner review 2026-10-16-learner-seven-v3.md: completed output means jobs passing every station; no empirical delegation claim.

claims.text: A toy owner handles 8 jobs/hour, the delegated handoff handles 6, and finishing handles 12. Steady output? Every completed job needs the handoff, so min(8,6,12) = 6 jobs/hour.
claims.source: Original transfer toy, flow, inputs [8, 6, 12], output 6; independent Python recomputation.
